title: Computer security
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to build and evaluate secure systems: security principles and threat modeling, memory-safety vulnerabilities and defenses, symmetric and public-key cryptography, hashes, MACs and signatures, certificates and TLS, authentication and password storage, access control, web security (injection, cross-site scripting, CSRF and sessions), network defenses, and secure development, responsible disclosure, ethics and law.
primary_reading: UC Berkeley CS 161 Computer Security textbook (free online)

weeks.2: Memory safety: buffer overflows and defenses
weeks.3: Symmetric cryptography and block cipher modes
weeks.9: Web security: SQL injection and cross-site scripting
weeks.10: Web security: CSRF, sessions and the same-origin policy
weeks.11: Network security: firewalls, intrusion detection and denial of service
weeks.12: Secure development, disclosure, ethics and law

blocks.deliverable: Choose the right primitive for five scenarios.
Week 7 midterm; design password storage with salts and slow hashing.
Fix injection and XSS bugs in supplied code.
Write a responsible-disclosure report for a supplied bug.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Security review: threat-model a supplied small web application, review its code for vulnerabilities, write fixes for at least three issues with tests that show each fix works, and produce a professional security report with risk ratings.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
